description: Computer software is broadly categorized into two main types. System Software manages and controls the computer hardware, while Application Software is designed to perform specific tasks for the end-user.

sections.title: Basic Types of Software
sections.description: Definitions and core classifications of computer software.

key_concepts.explanation: A set of instructions, data, or programs used to operate computers and execute specific tasks. It is the intangible component that makes hardware functional.
Software designed to manage the computer's hardware and provide a platform for running application software. It acts as an interface between the user and the hardware.
Software designed to help the user perform specific, single, or multiple related tasks. It is highly dependent on system software to execute.

sections.title: Key Components of System Software
sections.description: The various types of system software that handle foundational computing operations.

key_concepts.explanation: The most crucial system software that manages hardware resources, memory, and processes. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android.
Specialized programs that allow the operating system to communicate seamlessly with attached hardware devices like printers, keyboards, and graphics cards.
Programs designed to help analyze, configure, optimize, or maintain a computer system. Examples: Antivirus scanners, Disk Defragmenters, Backup utilities.
System programs that convert human-readable high-level programming language code into machine code (0s and 1s) that the CPU can execute. Examples: Compilers, Interpreters, Assemblers.

sections.title: Types of Application Software
sections.description: Categories of software designed to fulfill everyday user requirements.

key_concepts.explanation: Software created to meet the common needs of the general public. Examples: Word Processors (MS Word), Spreadsheets (MS Excel), Web Browsers (Google Chrome, Firefox).
Software custom-built exclusively for a specific organization or a highly specialized task. Examples: Railway Reservation Systems, Payroll Management Systems, Banking Software.

sections.title: Key Comparisons and Differences
sections.description: Technical and functional differences between System and Application software.

key_associations.associated_with: System software is built for the hardware; Application software is built for the user.
key_associations.extra_info: System software operates mostly in the background, whereas users interact directly with application software.

key_associations.associated_with: Application software cannot run without System software.
key_associations.extra_info: System software can run completely independently of application software.

key_associations.associated_with: System software is typically written in low-level languages (Assembly, C), while Application software uses high-level languages (Java, Python, C#).
key_associations.extra_info: Low-level languages allow for direct hardware manipulation and memory management.

key_associations.associated_with: System software starts executing automatically when the computer is turned on (booting).
key_associations.extra_info: Application software executes only when the user explicitly launches or requests it.

sections.title: Important Exam Facts
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts related to software concepts frequently asked in exams.

important_facts.fact: System Software is mandatory for a computer to boot and function, whereas Application Software is completely optional based on user needs.
Firmware is a specific class of system software that provides low-level control for a device's specific hardware and is permanently embedded in Read-Only Memory (ROM), such as the BIOS.
A Compiler translates the entire source code into machine code in a single batch, whereas an Interpreter translates and executes the code line-by-line.
Microsoft Office is NOT an operating system or system software; it is an Application Suite comprising multiple general-purpose application programs.
